headline: OGILVY CAN NOW PUT CAA'S ACTORS AND ATHLETES IN BRAND ADVERTS WITHOUT THEM TURNING UP, AT 65 TO 75 PERCENT LESS PER ASSET, AND THE THING THAT MADE IT POSSIBLE IS NOT THE AI.  IT IS A SCANNING ROOM WITH 204 CAMERAS THAT CAA BUILT FOUR YEARS AGO
deck: Ogilvy and CAA announced a product called Echo yesterday.  It makes advertising featuring AI generated versions of CAA's roster, and Ogilvy expects it to produce more assets, faster, at 65 to 75 percent lower cost per asset.  Read the detail and the story changes shape.  The scans have existed for four years.  What arrived this week is the permission to use them.
tldr: Ogilvy and CAA launched Echo, which makes brand adverts starring AI replicas of CAA's roster at an expected 65 to 75 percent lower cost per asset, and the reason it is possible now is a four-year-old scanning facility plus a new rights framework rather than new AI.  Ask any talent agency you brief whether a licensed scan exists, who approves each asset, and which markets are cleared, before you discuss money.

Somebody Feed Phil moved from Netflix to free YouTube with United Airlines as title sponsor of its eight-episode ninth season, and Rosenthal says United supplies crew and equipment and removes the hassle of landing with kit in foreign countries.  List what your brand owns that a production would otherwise rent, price it as a sponsorship contribution, and take that list to your next creator conversation.

YouTube changed its view count in August so a view now registers the moment playback starts, and advertisers responded by demanding engaged views and link clicks before signing creator deals.  Price your next creator contract against their trailing 30-day median with the outliers removed, which is what the agency HYDP does, and define engaged views in writing because nobody agrees yet.

A League of Legends semifinal peaked at 3,592,042 concurrent viewers on Sunday, while co-streaming grew 19.7 percent last quarter as official viewing declined, and MPL Malaysia's season peak rose above 700,000 while its average audience fell 47.66 percent.  Insist every live audience figure you accept carries peak and average concurrents together, and watch the 14 November final on creator co-streams to see the buy you will be offered next season.

The Trade Desk reported 736 million dollars, down 0.5 percent, cut 15 percent of staff and guided Q4 about 11 percent below last year, while saying video including connected television is now more than half its revenue mix, and Zeta, Viant and PubMatic all grew.  Take the majority-video mix figure into your budget conversation and ask what share of your own digital spend is video.

Viant bought the AI advert generator Waymark for 20 million dollars in cash, citing data that fresh creative lifts attention more than 80 percent among over-exposed viewers, which says the shortage in connected television is versions of the advert rather than places to run it.  Pull your frequency report this week and build three alternate cuts from footage you already own.

One in four Americans believe creators consistently disclose paid deals, while 14 percent of creators say they do not always disclose and 18 percent say a brand asked them not to in the past year, and Boomers are the group that notices.  Put a disclosure requirement in your creator contract template, tell your partners it is there, and audit every live campaign for a visible disclosure this week.
